title: Dinner Without a Plot
angle: A familiar meal can offer comfort precisely because it asks for no novelty, turning repetition into ease rather than a failure of imagination.
paragraphs: A familiar dinner has a quiet advantage: nobody needs to work out what it is trying to be. The same soup, sandwich, or plate of eggs can show up again without a new backstory. You know roughly how it will taste, and that predictability can feel like a small kindness at the end of an ordinary day.

Meals often get treated as occasions that ought to surprise us, even on a Tuesday when the main ambition is to eat something decent. But novelty is not the only measure of pleasure. Familiar food can free the meal from performance. There is less to assess, compare, or explain; the attention can settle on the eating itself, or drift toward whoever happens to be nearby.

Of course, repetition can become dull, and a change of flavor can be welcome. The point is not to make a virtue out of eating the same thing forever. It is simply that an unremarkable dinner need not apologize for being unremarkable. Sometimes the best thing a meal offers is the comfort of knowing what comes next—and then being allowed to enjoy it.
